extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider:** Azure only.
- **Regions / zones:** No region or availability-zone data is present; **no HA/resilience topology is evidenced**.
- **Deployment path:** GitHub Actions workflow named **“Deploy to Azure”**.
- **Triggers:** `push` and `workflow_dispatch`, which expands the execution surface to both repository changes and manual runs.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret store in use:** `github_actions_secret`.
- **Credential handling:** Azure access is tied to `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`.
- **Risk:** No plaintext secret is shown, but this is **static secret-based authentication**, not federated OIDC. That increases exposure to secret leakage, rotation drift, and workflow misuse.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption-at-rest coverage:** `false` in the aggregate signals.
- **Key management:** No KMS/CMK/rotation details are provided.
- **Risk:** There is **no evidence of at-rest encryption coverage** or any key governance controls in the supplied configuration.

### 4) IAM / least-privilege
- **IAM type:** `managed_identity`.
- **Scope:** `subscription`.
- **Trust principal:** `github-actions`.
- **Risk:** Subscription-level scope is **broad** and may exceed least-privilege needs unless the deployment truly spans the full subscription.
- **OIDC:** Not used (`uses_oidc: false`), so there is **no federated workload identity**; auth relies on stored GitHub secret material.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runner:** `ubuntu-latest` GitHub-hosted runner.
- **Security implications:** The runner is ephemeral, but the use of a mutable “latest” label means the underlying image can change over time.
- **Trigger surface:** `push` + `workflow_dispatch` increases the chance of unintended or unauthorized deployment execution if repository controls are weak.
- **OIDC gap:** No OIDC federation is configured, so CI/CD authentication is not using short-lived cloud-issued credentials.

### 6) Container security
- **Not evidenced in provided data.** No container nodes or workload specs were supplied, so root/non-root, health checks, and resource limits **cannot be assessed** from this configuration.

### 7) Key risks and prioritized recommendations
1. **Replace static Azure credentials with GitHub Actions OIDC federation.** This removes long-lived cloud secrets from GitHub and reduces credential theft risk.
2. **Reduce Azure IAM scope from subscription-level to the minimum required resource scope.** Use resource-group or workload-specific permissions where possible.
3. **Define and verify encryption-at-rest and secret governance.** Confirm storage/services are encrypted, establish key ownership/rotation, and review GitHub secret access controls for the workflow.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry points:** FastAPI exposes `Login`, `Me`, `Logout`, and `Chat Endpoint`; `Bearer Auth` protects all of them, plus `Generic`.
- **Orchestration:** `OpenAI Agents` is the main runtime that calls the `Cancellation`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, `Seat Booking`, and `Triage` agents, and can also call all listed tools directly.
- **Agent routing:** `Triage Agent` delegates to `Flight Status Agent` and `FAQ Agent`.
- **Model use:** `gpt-4.1-mini` is used by the `Relevance Guardrail`, `Jailbreak Guardrail`, and all five agents.
- **Tool access:** Agents can call `Baggage Tool`, `Cancel Flight`, `Display Seat Map`, `Faq Lookup Tool`, and `Flight Status Tool`; `OpenAI Agents` can also call `Lookup Reservation` and `Update Seat`.
- **Data stores:** `Sqlite` is shown with **no connections**, so the graph does not show any reachable datastore.
- **Security observations:** Tool calls are broadly exposed through `OpenAI Agents`, with no explicit guardrail links shown to endpoints, agents, or tools. The graph shows guardrail components, but not where they are enforced.
